info.title: Switchboard app API
info.description: REST and long-polls for the Switchboard phone apps. Approvals need a device signature; denials need only a device token.

its Herdr session. It then leaves the session list.

put.summary:
Turns on this device's lock-screen card, or updates how to reach it. iOS sends its live key,
to which every board is sealed, and its card's push tokens; Android sends none.

delete.summary: Turns off this device's lock-screen card.

get.summary: What the lock-screen card shows: who needs you, who is running, how many are idle. Masked.
The ship buttons every paired phone shows, for all projects and per project.

put.summary: Replaces the ship buttons for all projects, or one project's own list.

get.summary:
What each agent did since a time: turns, dialogs, errors, approvals and sessions started, plus
its last line. Masked.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix ms: when this phone last had the app open.

post.summary: The same facts, summarised by `claude -p` with every tool off; only when the owner turned it on.

400.description: The summary is off, or the runner is too old

post.summary:
One message, routed as WhatsApp routes it: a named project starts a session there, `use <x>`
picks something running, and anything else goes to `current`.

200.description: Started, sent, a question, or a refusal with its reason

post.summary: Where `/messages` would send this text, without starting or sending anything.

get.summary: As the session's, for an agent Switchboard didn't start.
The dialog on any agent's screen, Switchboard's or not, with its options.

post.summary:
Picks one offered option. The deny needs no signature, and nor does a `provisional` option,
which only moves to the next question of a group; any other option needs the device's
signature over the answer message.

409.description: The dialog changed or was answered; read it again

504.description: The Enter may have been sent; never retried

post.summary:
Shows the previous question of a group again, when the dialog says `can_go_back`. It submits
nothing, so it needs no signature.

400.description: There is no earlier question to show

409.description: The dialog changed; read it again

get.summary:
Resolves a `waiting` push's attention id. Open only while the agent still shows that
occurrence, so an expired or moved-on one never leads to a replacement agent.

Activity.description: What agents did since a time, from facts the hub records; no model involved.

agents.description: Who needs you first, then the most recent.

summary_on.description: The owner turned on the `claude -p` summary.

AgentActivityView.description: The first line of the last thing an agent said or did, as a tile shows it.

name.description: As in `AgentView`; for a session's agent, its Herdr name.

session_id.description: Set when the agent is a session's.

line.description:
At most about 200 characters, masked. Absent when the agent has said nothing yet.
Untrusted text.

at.description: When the line was written, as an RFC 3339 time from the agent's log.

dialog.description: None when the screen shows no dialog Switchboard recognises; show the screen instead.

waiting.description:
The agent is waiting on its owner. With no `dialog`, it waits on something the phone
can't show as options: say so and offer the screen. Absent from older hubs.

AgentView.description:
A Herdr agent Switchboard didn't start. It has no permission hooks, so its dialogs
are answered in Herdr.

name.description:
`<herdr session>/<agent>` when the machine runs several Herdr sessions. An agent without
a Herdr name goes by its pane id, e.g. `mono1/w1:p2`.

kind.description: e.g. `claude` or `codex`, as Herdr reports it.

title.description: Its terminal title, usually what it's working on. Untrusted text.

space.description: The label of the Herdr workspace (space) it runs in. Untrusted text.

backend.description:
`herdr` for a Herdr TUI agent, `hc` for one in the Herdr app, named `hc/<agent>`. Older
hubs leave it out.

space_id.description:
The id of the space it runs in, as on a session. Absent from an older hub or runner, and
for an agent in the Herdr app outside every space.

can_rename.description:
`POST /agents/rename` can rename it. False for one in the Herdr app whose name was fixed
when it started or that shares its tab; rename those at the machine. Older hubs leave
it out.

ended.description:
Agents Switchboard didn't start that ended in the last day, latest first. Older hubs
leave it out.

activity.description:
With `activity=true`: every agent's last line, sessions' agents included, on the machines
in `activity_machines`, one entry per agent. Older hubs leave it out.

activity_machines.description:
With `activity=true`: the machines `activity` covers. For an agent on any other machine,
read its conversation instead.

kind.description:
`permission`, `question` (Claude's AskUserQuestion) or `plan` (plan approval). A question
is answered with the ids of its chosen options, a plan with its one option `allow`.

input_text.description: The masked tool input as text: a shell command, or the input as JSON.

questions.description: For a question, each question's text.

question_options.description: For a question, each question with its options.

deadline.description: Unix milliseconds; unanswered by then means denied.

multi_select.description: More than one option may be chosen.

state.description: `open`, `answered`, `gone` (the agent moved on or was replaced) or `expired`.

dialog.description: While open, the dialog it waits at, if one is recognised.

same_agent.description:
Whether the agent now under `agent` is the one that asked. False once it ended or another
agent took the name, so a client shouldn't open it; left out when the hub can't tell.

state.description: Now: `waiting`, `error`, `working` or `idle`, when the hub has seen it.

last_reply.description: The first line of the last thing it said, masked.

AwaySettingsView.description: "While you were away" choices, kept on the hub.

summary.description: Summarise with `claude -p` on the owner's Claude account, every tool off. Off by default.

reason.description:
Why it can't be chosen: `not_answering` (the Herdr app isn't open there), `not_followed`
(its runner follows no Herdr app) or `runner_too_old` (its runner can't be told).

expires_at.description: Unix milliseconds; part of the signed message.

ChangedFile.description: One file a session changed since it started.

added.description: Lines added; absent for a binary or new untracked file.

binary.description: A binary file: its diff shows its size only. Absent means false.

size.description: Bytes, for a binary file still in the worktree.

truncated.description: More files changed than are listed.

nonce.description: Required to allow: the nonce from the approval's challenge.

signature.description:
Required to allow: DER ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 of the approval message, base64url,
made with the approval key. For a permission (version 1) the message is
`switchboard-approval-v1`, then `hub=`, `device=`, `approval=`, `decision=allow`,
`nonce=`, `expires=` lines, joined by `\n`. For a question or plan (version 3) it is the
answer message: `switchboard-answer-v1`, then `hub=`, `device=`, `target=approval:<id>`,
`occurrence=<id>`, `option=` (the choices joined by `,`), `label=` (SHA-256 hex of the
chosen labels joined by `\n`), `request=`, `nonce=`, `expires=`.

choices.description:
For a question, the chosen option ids, one per question (several for a multi-select);
a plan's only option is `allow`.

outcome.description: The recorded outcome, `allow` or `deny`. An allow that never reached the agent is a deny.

replayed.description: Already decided; nothing was sent again.

kept_because.description: Why the worktree was kept: uncommitted or unmerged work, or a failed removal.

Dialog.description: A dialog on an agent's screen. Masked; the ids are opaque.

kind.description: `question`, `plan`, `permission`, or `other` for a list no recogniser knows.

selected.description: The option the screen has selected.

answerable.description: It can be answered from the phone now; otherwise answer it in Herdr.

reason.description:
Why not: `read_only`, `hooked` (answered as an approval instead),
`hook_pending`, `hook_failed`, `not_blocked` or `answered`.

steps.description:
When the agent asked several questions together: one per question, in order, to show as
tabs. Claude's ends with its `Submit` tab. Empty otherwise, and absent from older hubs.

can_go_back.description:
The group's previous question can be shown again, with `/agents/dialog/back`. Absent
from older hubs.

request_id.description: Replays return the recorded outcome; required with a signature.

nonce.description: Required for any option but the deny: the nonce from the dialog's challenge.

signature.description: DER ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 of the answer message, base64url, by the approval key.

outcome.description: `answered`: the dialog closed after the Enter.

replayed.description: Already answered with this request id; nothing was sent again.

next.description:
The dialog the screen shows after the answer, such as the next question of a group, which
saves reading it again. Absent when nothing shows, on a replay, and from older hubs.

occurrence_id.description: The dialog being shown, so a stale tap moves nothing.

dialog.description:
The dialog now showing, which saves reading it again. Absent when the hub's runner didn't
say; read the dialog then.

DialogChallenge.description:
What an answer signs, as `switchboard-answer-v1` (message version 3): `hub=`, `device=`,
`target=agent:<machine_id>/<agent>`, `occurrence=`, `option=`, `label=` (the option's
`label_sha256`), `request=`, `nonce=`, `expires=` lines, joined by `\n`.

label_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex of `label`; an answer signs and repeats it.

offered.description: It may be chosen from the phone; the others are shown for context.

provisional.description:
It answers one question of a group and submits nothing, so it needs no signature either.
The choice that submits the group is signed. Absent from older hubs.

DialogStep.description: One question of a group asked together.

label.description: The agent's short name for the question, or its number.

answered.description: It has an answer already. Codex doesn't say, so its steps are never marked.

current.description:
The dialog shows this one now. Claude marks its open tab only in colour, so there it is
the first unanswered question, and no step is marked when that can't be told.

lines.description: With up to 25 unchanged lines around each change; the app folds long runs.

cut.description: The hunk was too long for one page and is cut short.

old.description: Its number in the old file; absent for an added line.

new.description: Its number in the new file; absent for a deleted line.

EndedAgent.description: An agent that has left its pane. Sessions Switchboard started keep their own records.

name.description: Its name when it ended, as in `AgentView`.

title.description: Its last terminal title. Untrusted text.

space.description:
The Herdr workspace or Herdr app space it last ran in, as in `AgentView`. Untrusted
text. Absent for one that ended before spaces were recorded, and from older hubs.

started_at.description: When the hub first saw it, in milliseconds.

operation_id.description: Set with `outcome_unknown`: look the request up later by its request id.

FileDiffView.description: A page of one changed file's unified diff since the session started. Read-only, masked.

next.description: Pass as `from` for the next page; absent on the last.

withheld.description: The file is the kind that holds secrets (an env file or a key), so nothing of it is shown.

at.description: Unix seconds the board was built.

waiting.description: Longest wait first, at most two.

running_more.description: Running agents beyond the named ones.

finished.description: An agent that finished within the last minute.

LiveMode.description: When a phone's lock-screen card shows.

live_key.description: iOS: the P-256 key-agreement key boards are sealed to, SEC1 uncompressed, base64url.

start_token.description: iOS 17.2 and later: the push-to-start token, as hex.

activity_token.description: iOS: the running card's update token, as hex; null when no card is running.

activity_started_at.description: Unix seconds the running card started.

mode.description: When the card shows; `working` when absent.

since.description: Unix seconds it has waited since.

error.description: It stopped on an error rather than asking.

project_id.description: Set for a project to start in.

target.description: Set for something running to send to.

MessagePreview.description: Where a message would go, without sending it.

message.description: What sending would do, or the question sending would ask, in a sentence.

machine_id.description: For `start`: the machine it would run on.

current.description: Where text that names no project goes.

request_id.description: Required, one per draft: a retried send with the same id is not sent twice.

current.description: Where text that names no project goes.

project_id.description: Answers a `choose_project`: start in this project.

target.description: Answers a `choose_target`: send to this one.

message.description: What happened, or the question to answer, in a sentence.

current.description: Where text that names no project goes from now on.

min_client_build.description: The oldest app build this hub still serves; older builds should ask to be updated.

message_version.description: The signed message version the hub accepts.

max_wait_ms.description: The longest long-poll wait the hub honours.

text.description: The agent's terminal text, masked. Untrusted: it's the agent's, not Switchboard's.

ansi.description:
The same screen with its colours as ANSI SGR codes, when asked for and when it shows
exactly `text`. Left out when masking changed the screen, or by older hubs and runners.

code.description: The single-use code from `switchboard admin pair-device`.

name.description: Shown in the devices list, e.g. "Adarsh's iPhone".

auth_key.description: P-256 public key, SEC1 uncompressed, base64url without padding. Signs token challenges.

approval_key.description: Same encoding. Signs approvals; the phone keeps it behind Face ID or the passcode.

fingerprint.description: Show this; the admin confirms the terminal shows the same.

token.description:
The APNs device token as hex, or the FCM registration token; null turns push off for
this device.

environment.description: For APNs; an FCM token ignores it.

provider.description: Which service the token is for; Apple's when absent.

name.description:
In a Herdr terminal: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, at
most 32. In the Herdr app: as for a session, since it names the agent's tab.

request_id.description: A lost response can be retried with this id.

RenameResponse.description: The name as it is now listed; for a session, its label.

RenameSessionRequest.description: A new name: one line of 1 to 40 characters, without `/`. Masked like any other text.

herdr_session.description: The `herdr_session` of the session or agent that listed the space; `hc` for the Herdr app.

label.description: Project plus the first four characters of the id, as WhatsApp shows it.

hook_failed.description: Stuck at a dialog the runner won't answer; answer it in Herdr.

notifies.description: False when muted or when mute-all is on.

herdr_session.description: The Herdr session it runs in; `herdr session attach <name>` opens it on the machine.

backend.description: `herdr` for a Herdr TUI session, `hc` for one in the Herdr app. Older hubs leave it out.

space.description:
The Herdr app space, or Herdr workspace, its agent was last seen in, as in `AgentView`.
Untrusted text. Absent until the hub has seen it, and from older hubs.

space_id.description:
That space's id on its machine, for `POST /spaces/rename` and a start's `space_id`.
Absent until the hub has seen it, from an older hub or runner, and for an agent in the
Herdr app outside every space.

can_rename.description: `POST /sessions/{id}/rename` can name it. Older hubs leave it out.

revision.description: Pass back as `after_revision` to wait for the next change.

scope.description: `*` for all projects, or a project id.

buttons.description: In order; an empty list removes a project's own list.

ShipButtonView.description: A button on a finished agent that asks it to run one of its own skills.

skill.description: As the agent runs it: `/pr` for Claude Code, `$pr` for a Codex skill. A bare name gets `/`.

after_pr.description: Shown only once the agent's reply names a pull request.

all.description: For every project without its own list. The first that isn't after-PR is the main one.

projects.description: Projects with their own list, which replaces `all` there.

Skill.description: A skill or command, as typed: `/name`, or `$name` for a Codex skill.

StartOptions.description: Where a new session on one machine opens, and what the New session screen may choose.

default.description:
`hc` (the Herdr app) or `herdr` (a Herdr terminal session): where a start with no
`backend` opens now. Absent when the machine's runner is too old to say.

machine_id.description: Defaults to the hub's default machine.

agent.description: `claude` or `codex`; defaults to the project's agent.

request_id.description: Required: a lost response can be looked up, or retried, by this id.

backend.description:
Where it opens on the machine: `hc` for the Herdr app, `herdr` for a Herdr terminal
session. Omitted, the machine's runner chooses as it always has. A choice the machine
can't serve fails with `backend_unavailable`; it never falls back or moves machine.

space_id.description:
A Herdr app space, by the `space_id` a session or agent listed, for the session's tab to
open in instead of a new space. Only with the Herdr app: with `backend` `herdr` it is a
bad request. A space that has gone fails with `not_found` before anything is created.

outcome.description:
`started`; `deduplicated` when the same start ran in the last minute ("already running");
`replayed` for a retried request id; `reconciled` when a lost reply was settled.

remove_worktree_if_clean.description: Removes the worktree only if it is clean and merged.

TargetRef.description:
Something a message can go to: a session by id, or an agent Switchboard didn't start by
machine and name.

signature.description:
DER ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 of the token message, base64url. The message is
`switchboard-token-v1`, then `hub=`, `device=`, `nonce=`, `expires=` lines, joined by `\n`.

Transcript.description:
Part of an agent's conversation, read from its own log; Claude agents only. Untrusted text,
masked.

items.description:
Oldest first. An item whose id was seen before replaces it: a tool call comes again
with its result.

start.description: Pass as `before` for the page before this one; 0 means it's the first.

end.description:
Pass as `after` for what comes next. A page asked for with `after` that doesn't start
there skipped some: replace what's shown instead of appending.

queued.description:
Messages waiting for the agent to take them in, oldest first, as of `end`: what to show
as queued now, replacing any shown before. Only on pages that reach the conversation's
end; absent when none wait. Older hubs leave it out.

kind.description:
`user`, `assistant`, `tool`, `note`, or `peer` for a message another terminal sent the
agent. Show a kind you don't know as a note.

text.description:
What was said, in Markdown; for a tool, a one-line summary. Absent on a tool result
whose call is on an earlier page.

input.description: The tool's input as JSON, shortened.

added.description: Lines an edit adds and removes, when its input says. Older hubs leave them out.

ends_turn.description:
The reply the agent ended its turn with: its answer, even when work follows that something
else started. Older hubs leave it out.

from.description: Who sent a `peer` message: the sending terminal's agent name, else its id.
